summary: The most-viewed talk episode on the channel, and the comments show why: the guest brought his own organised fandom. Nicky Nachat's followers self-identify as 'แก๊งขาหื่น', announce which channel they came from, and run explicit view-count campaigns because the guest promised rewards at milestones — a boat trip at 2M, a Japan trip at 3M — with commenters reporting each threshold as it is passed. The second and equally large cluster is retroactive shipping: the pair later dated in real life, so viewers return to re-read the episode as evidence, timestamping blushes and physical contact, and a later wave returns again after the relationship ends, which gives a handful of openly sad comments. Rewatching is heavy and self-reported, ten or more times for many. A distinct cluster uses the comments as a guest-request board, naming Oat Pramote, Lee Thanat and Tor Thanapob and asking others to upvote.

audience_signals: The guest's own fandom is the acquisition engine for talk episodes — commenters state which channel they arrived from, giving a traceable referral path
Reward-gated view targets work: the guest's public promise at 2M/3M/4M produced self-organised, self-reported view campaigns and is a repeatable growth mechanic
Real-life romance converted this episode into an evergreen asset — rewatch waves are keyed to later news events (dating reveal, EP100, breakup), so old episodes keep earning views
The comment section operates as a fandom home base with its own name and in-group identity, not just a reaction space
An explicit, upvote-ranked guest demand list already exists in the comments and can be read as a booking backlog
Chemistry, not the format, is what viewers rewatch — the questions are secondary to reading the hosts' reactions
